answer: Escrowed reputation carryover: an identity’s score transfers only through a slow decay curve, so newcomers start near zero and each clone inherits nothing. A mirror of past transactions gates withdrawals, requiring the attacker to fund real activity for months before any clone can extract value. Withdrawal fees pay honest operators a copper rebate, making legitimate history cheaper than parallel fabrication. Each clone thus burns the nectar of genuine trade volume—concrete cost: months of fees and lost rebates per identity, far exceeding one honest operator’s total expense.
